extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI)
extraction.description: A multimodal benchmark for evaluating large multimodal models on detecting self-contradictory or conflicting instructions. It contains 20,000 conflicting instructions across 8 tasks, evenly split between language-language and vision-language paradigms.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, and Dequan Wang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created using an automatic framework called AutoCreate that starts from a small batch of manually input seeds and iteratively generates data through language and visual loops with a generator, decorator, and cleaner. Large language models and programs were used to generate and decorate examples with self-contradictions, low-quality data was removed, and both human experts and LLMs double-checked quality before refined outputs were fed back into the seed pool. One task, SemanticConflict, additionally reused ImageNet images by retrieving images for labels and substituting labels in generated questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw/source data included manually input task-relevant seeds in a seed pool, generated language and vision data, and for SemanticConflict, external ImageNet images retrieved by label.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The benchmark was created through an automatic dataset creation framework (AutoCreate) using generators, decorators, and cleaners, with quality double-checking by both human experts and LLMs; human experts also rigorously checked the final dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality control involved double-checking by both human experts and LLMs, and the final AutoCreate-generated dataset was rigorously checked by human experts.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Large language models were used in the automatic dataset creation framework AutoCreate to generate data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is limited to language-language and vision-language paradigms, lacks fine-grained control over conflict degree, and does not include a detailed study of LMM attention mechanisms under conflicting instructions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to help researchers and practitioners assess and improve LMM handling of conflicting instructions, advance human-computer interaction, promote inclusivity in AI research through diverse instruction datasets, and improve trust and reliability of AI systems for societal integration.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed as a benchmark to evaluate large multimodal models' ability to detect and comprehend conflicting instructions, and to facilitate qualitative evaluation through different splits.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand the benchmark to include more modalities in the future using the AutoCreate framework.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data were augmented and subset-selected after generation: OCRConflict images varied in font, size, and color to increase diversity; FigureConflict charts used random style options; SCI-Base and SCI-Core were manually selected subsets of 10% and 1% of SCI-All.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Generated data were cleaned and filtered through a cleaner that removed data not meeting quality standards, followed by quality checks and double-checking by human experts and LLMs.

description.evidence: We introduce the Self-Contradictory Instructions benchmark to evaluate the capability of LMMs in recognizing conflicting commands. It comprises 20,000 conflicts, evenly distributed between language and vision paradigms.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Limitations To begin with, we only include language-language and vision-language paradigms. More modalities will be included in our SCI benchmark based on our automatic framework, AutoCreate. Besides, no fine-grained control is introduced to determine the conflict degree. Finally, we do not provide a detailed study on the attention mechanism of large multimodal models when confronted with conflict instructions.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Social Impact Our work on the SCI benchmark, along with the AutoCreate framework and CaP approach, has significant social implications. It provides researchers and practitioners with a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs’ ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction and communication technologies... promoting inclusivity in AI research... By improving dissonance detection, our approach boosts LMM performance and fosters trust and reliability in AI systems, essential for societal integration.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: Hence, we propose a multimodal benchmark, Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI), to evaluate the ability of LMMs to detect conflicted instructions... We have rigorously guaranteed the quality of SCI and manually provide three levels of splits according to the occurring frequency of conflict types, SCI-Core (1%), SCI-Base (10%), and SCI-All (100%), to facilitate qualitative evaluation.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: More modalities will be included in our SCI benchmark based on our automatic framework, AutoCreate.
